# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites

## Context

Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").

**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
is still a real (if minor) UX gap.

**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.

The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.

## Changes

### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point

Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
`RunState`:

```swift
/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
/// SIGHUP'ing it.
@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
```

Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
both views will call:

```swift
/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
@discardableResult
func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
  -> TerminalTab
{
  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
  }
  return tab
}
```

Update `hasLiveRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:2257`) to also check live Investigate tabs, reusing
the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:

```swift
var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
    }
}
```

In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
doesn't linger:

```swift
ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
```

Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.

### 2. `TerminalStatusBar.swift:326-332` — route through the new method

Replace the direct `addRunTab` call in the `onInvestigate` closure:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd = state?.view.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: bannerState, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tabID)
  showingDiagnosis = false
},
```

(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here.)

### 3. `TerminalTabStrip.swift:436-441` — fix bug 2 and route through the new method

Replace the hardcoded `"claude"` + direct `addRunTab` call:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd = tab.surface?.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: state, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tab.id)
  agentPopoverTab = nil
},
```

(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here; `state` is the `AgentBannerState`
already bound by the enclosing `if let state = agentManager.banners[tab.id]`. `tab.surface`
(`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) already collapses the `if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content`
match — no need to hand-roll it again, matching the status-bar site's `state?.view` shape.)

This fixes bug 2 (both sites now build the identical seeded command via
`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`) and closes bug 1 (both sites now go through
`AppStore`, which owns the tracking, restoring `addRunTab`'s documented caller contract).

### 4. `TerminalSessions.swift:945-952` — doc note

Add one line to `addRunTab`'s doc comment noting Investigate sessions are tracked in
`AppStore.investigateTabs`, not `runStates`, so the split is explicit at the definition too (not
just at the call sites) — closes the issue's "or a comment explaining why" fallback for the part
that *is* staying a deliberate design choice (no cross-window dedup, no supervisor/pidfile).

## Verification

- `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests.swift` — add:
  - A test asserting `startInvestigate` produces a tab whose command matches
    `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` for a given `AgentBannerState`, and that
    `investigateTabs[tab.id] == target.id` afterward — covers "both call sites build the same
    command line" (the issue's suggested unit check) by construction, since both now call the
    one method.
  - A test that `hasLiveRunCommand` is `false` before `startInvestigate`, `true` while the tab's
    surface reports a live process, and `false` again after simulating `onChildExited` and
    (separately) after simulating tab removal — two independent cleanup paths, both must be
    tested (mirrors the existing `testGracefullyStopAllWaitsForEveryLiveCommandThenCompletes` /
    `testReapClearsRunState` style already in this file).
  - A test that `gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` completes immediately (no hang) when the only
    live process is an Investigate tab and `runStates` is empty — this exact combination
    (`hasLiveRunCommand == true` via `investigateTabs`, but nothing in `runStates` to iterate) is
    new with this change; the existing `testGracefullyStopAllCompletesImmediatelyWhenNothingLive`
    only covers the "nothing at all is live" case.
- `make app-lint` / `make app-format` on the touched files.
- `make app-test` (or scoped `xcodebuild -only-testing:WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests`) green.
- Manual, per the issue's own verification section:
  - Fail a command, open Investigate from the status bar and from the tab-strip chip — confirm
    both agents start with the failure context (the prompt text, not a bare `claude`).
  - Start Investigate, then close the *window* (⌘W the window / red close button, not the tab)
    with "confirm on quit" enabled — confirm the close-confirmation now fires for the live agent
    instead of silently killing it. **Note:** ⌘Q (app quit) is intentionally NOT part of this
    check — `stopRunCommandsThenTerminate` (`WorkroomApp.swift:627-646`) shows no alert at all,
    for any live run command, and that's unchanged here: sending a stop signal to an interactive
    `claude` REPL and waiting for a "clean exit" has no defined meaning the way it does for a
    supervised dev-server (which traps SIGTERM to release a port) — extending quit-time
    protection to Investigate sessions is out of scope for this issue (see "NOT in scope" below).

# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites

## Context

Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").

**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
is still a real (if minor) UX gap.

**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.

The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.

## Changes

### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point

Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
`RunState`:

```swift
/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
/// SIGHUP'ing it.
///
///        runStates                    investigateTabs
///   [TargetID: RunState]          [TabID: TargetID]
///   one slot per target      many tabs allowed per target
///   (dev-server run)              (interactive claude)
///            │                            │
///            └─────────────┬──────────────┘
///                          ▼
///               hasLiveRunCommand (OR)
///                          │
///              ┌───────────┴────────────┐
///              ▼                        ▼
///   windowShouldClose confirm   stopRunCommandsThenTerminate (⌘Q)
///   alert — now fires for a     — unaffected in practice: only
///   live Investigate session    `runStates` feeds the actual
///                                gracefully-stop loop
@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
```

Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
both views will call:

```swift
/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
@discardableResult
func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
  -> TerminalTab
{
  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
  }
  return tab
}
```

Update `hasLiveRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:2257`) to also check live Investigate tabs, reusing
the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:

```swift
var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
    }
}
```

In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
doesn't linger:

```swift
ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
```

Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.

### 2. `TerminalStatusBar.swift:326-332` — route through the new method

Replace the direct `addRunTab` call in the `onInvestigate` closure:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd = state?.view.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: bannerState, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tabID)
  showingDiagnosis = false
},
```

(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here.)

### 3. `TerminalTabStrip.swift:436-441` — fix bug 2 and route through the new method

Replace the hardcoded `"claude"` + direct `addRunTab` call:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd = tab.surface?.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: state, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tab.id)
  agentPopoverTab = nil
},
```

(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here; `state` is the `AgentBannerState`
already bound by the enclosing `if let state = agentManager.banners[tab.id]`. `tab.surface`
(`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) already collapses the `if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content`
match — no need to hand-roll it again, matching the status-bar site's `state?.view` shape.)

This fixes bug 2 (both sites now build the identical seeded command via
`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`) and closes bug 1 (both sites now go through
`AppStore`, which owns the tracking, restoring `addRunTab`'s documented caller contract).

### 4. `TerminalSessions.swift:945-952` — doc note

Add one line to `addRunTab`'s doc comment noting Investigate sessions are tracked in
`AppStore.investigateTabs`, not `runStates`, so the split is explicit at the definition too (not
just at the call sites) — closes the issue's "or a comment explaining why" fallback for the part
that *is* staying a deliberate design choice (no cross-window dedup, no supervisor/pidfile).

## Verification

- `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests.swift` — add:
  - A test asserting `startInvestigate` produces a tab whose command matches
    `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` for a given `AgentBannerState`, and that
    `investigateTabs[tab.id] == target.id` afterward — covers "both call sites build the same
    command line" (the issue's suggested unit check) by construction, since both now call the
    one method.
  - A test that `hasLiveRunCommand` is `false` before `startInvestigate`, `true` while the tab's
    surface reports a live process, and `false` again after simulating `onChildExited` and
    (separately) after simulating tab removal — two independent cleanup paths, both must be
    tested (mirrors the existing `testGracefullyStopAllWaitsForEveryLiveCommandThenCompletes` /
    `testReapClearsRunState` style already in this file).
  - A test that `gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` completes immediately (no hang) when the only
    live process is an Investigate tab and `runStates` is empty — this exact combination
    (`hasLiveRunCommand == true` via `investigateTabs`, but nothing in `runStates` to iterate) is
    new with this change; the existing `testGracefullyStopAllCompletesImmediatelyWhenNothingLive`
    only covers the "nothing at all is live" case.
- `make app-lint` / `make app-format` on the touched files.
- `make app-test` (or scoped `xcodebuild -only-testing:WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests`) green.

596	    // UI-test fixture quits cleanly (no modal, no waiting) so XCUITest teardown never blocks. The
597	    // session still flushes here: this branch IS terminating, and a UI test that relaunches to check
598	    // what was restored must not race the coalescing timer (issue #46).
599	    if UITestFixture.isActive {
600	      SessionCoordinator.shared.flushAndFreeze()
601	      return .terminateNow
602	    }
603	    if Defaults[.confirmOnQuit] {
604	      let alert = NSAlert()
605	      alert.messageText = "Quit Workroom?"
606	      alert.informativeText = "Quitting closes all terminals and stops any running processes."
607	      alert.addButton(withTitle: "Quit")
608	      alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
609	      alert.showsSuppressionButton = true
610	      alert.suppressionButton?.title = "Don't ask me again"
611	      let shouldQuit = alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn
612	      // Ticking the box stops future confirmations — whether they Quit or Cancel, the checkbox
613	      // means "stop asking". Writes the same key the menu/Settings toggles bind to.
614	      if alert.suppressionButton?.state == .on {
615	        Defaults[.confirmOnQuit] = false
616	      }
617	      guard shouldQuit else { return .terminateCancel }
618	    }
619	    return stopRunCommandsThenTerminate(sender)
620	  }
621	
622	  /// Ctrl-C any live run commands and let them exit before the process dies, so dev servers clean up
623	  /// (release their port + pidfile) instead of being orphaned by the OS hangup on exit — a SIGHUP
624	  /// that Puma ignores, surfacing as "A server is already running" on the next launch (issue #7).
625	  /// Sends only key events — never frees a surface — so the no-mass-free-on-quit rationale in
626	  /// `applicationWillTerminate` still holds. Bounded so a wedged server can't block the quit.
627	  @MainActor
628	  private func stopRunCommandsThenTerminate(_ sender: NSApplication) -> NSApplication.TerminateReply
629	  {
630	    let registry = WindowRegistry.shared
631	    // Mark the app as terminating so a window's own close handler doesn't also prompt/stop (#70).
632	    registry.isTerminating = true
633	    // Write the session and stop writing (issue #46). Deliberately HERE and not at the top of
634	    // `applicationShouldTerminate`: that method can still return `.terminateCancel` at the confirm
635	    // dialog, and freezing above that guard would silently kill session saving for the rest of the
636	    // app's life after one cancelled ⌘Q. This point is past the guard and still before any window
637	    // closes — which is exactly what the freeze protects, since the document is rebuilt from the
638	    // live windows.
639	    SessionCoordinator.shared.flushAndFreeze()
640	    guard registry.hasAnyLiveRunCommand else { return .terminateNow }
641	    // Stop every window's run commands, not just the focused one's.
642	    registry.gracefullyStopAllWindows(timeout: 5) {
643	      sender.reply(toApplicationShouldTerminate: true)
644	    }
645	    return .terminateLater
646	  }
647	
648	  /// Reactivation (Dock click, or clicking a notification while the app is inactive): bring an
649	  /// EXISTING window forward rather than letting AppKit open a brand-new one (issue #70). A
650	  /// value-based `WindowGroup` otherwise spawns a fresh window on reopen — so a notification click
651	  /// would pop a new window instead of returning to the window where the event happened (the
652	  /// notification handler then brings that specific owner window forward). Only ask AppKit to create
653	  /// a window when none exists.
654	  func applicationShouldHandleReopen(_ sender: NSApplication, hasVisibleWindows flag: Bool)
655	    -> Bool
656	  {
657	    let registry = WindowRegistry.shared
658	    if let window = registry.lastActiveStore?.hostWindow ?? registry.allStores.first?.hostWindow {
659	      window.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
660	      return false
661	    }
662	    return true
663	  }

666	  /// IO/render is still active races libghostty's surface teardown and crashes — EXC_BAD_ACCESS in
667	  /// `Surface.deinit`, or `os_unfair_lock` corruption in `Surface.handleMessage` — most readily when a
668	  /// run command's dev server (issue #7) is still busy. The process is exiting anyway: the OS reclaims
669	  /// libghostty's memory and closes the PTYs, so every child shell/server gets SIGHUP exactly as a
670	  /// manual `ghostty_surface_free` would deliver. (The per-workroom delete path still reaps a single

672	  ///
673	  /// Run commands are the exception that SIGHUP doesn't safely cover: a dev server like Puma ignores

questions.question: Correction: my earlier claim that "⌘Q shows no alert at all" was WRONG. WorkroomApp.swift:595-619 (applicationShouldTerminate) shows an UNCONDITIONAL "Quit Workroom? Quitting closes all terminals and stops any running processes." alert whenever confirmOnQuit is on (default), regardless of hasAnyLiveRunCommand — it already covers a live Investigate session today, no code change needed for that part. The ONLY real remaining gap is narrower: after the user clicks Quit, stopRunCommandsThenTerminate's graceful Ctrl-C-and-wait loop (gracefullyStopRuns) only touches runStates, so an Investigate tab gets zero graceful signal, just an immediate SIGHUP during teardown. Also relevant: AgentResumeCoordinator already offers to resume a killed agent session (claude --resume) in a restored pane next launch — so a quit-killed Investigate session isn't necessarily lost, just interrupted. Given this corrected picture, what should this issue's scope be?

Marginal benefit given the blanket dialog + resumability already cover the user-facing concern; adds real code + test surface for an edge case that's already soft-landed twice over.

1	# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
6	`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
7	`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
8	`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
9	`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
10	`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").
11	
12	**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
13	spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
14	it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
15	"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
16	right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
17	is still a real (if minor) UX gap.
18	
19	**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
20	`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
21	the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
22	whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.
23	
24	The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
25	value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
26	(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
27	must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
28	Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
29	call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.
30	
31	## Changes
32	
33	### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point
34	
35	Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
36	`RunState`:
37	
38	```swift
39	/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
40	/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
41	/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
42	/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
43	/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
44	/// SIGHUP'ing it.
45	///
46	///        runStates                    investigateTabs
47	///   [TargetID: RunState]          [TabID: TargetID]
48	///   one slot per target      many tabs allowed per target
49	///   (dev-server run)              (interactive claude)
50	///            │                            │
51	///            └─────────────┬──────────────┘
52	///                          ▼
53	///               hasLiveRunCommand (OR)
54	///                          │
55	///              ┌───────────┴────────────┐
56	///              ▼                        ▼
57	///   windowShouldClose confirm   stopRunCommandsThenTerminate (⌘Q)
58	///   alert — now fires for a     — unaffected in practice: only
59	///   live Investigate session    `runStates` feeds the actual
60	///                                gracefully-stop loop
61	@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
62	```
63	
64	Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
65	both views will call:
66	
67	```swift
68	/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
69	/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
70	/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
71	@discardableResult
72	func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
73	  -> TerminalTab
74	{
75	  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
76	  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
77	  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
78	  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
79	    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
80	  }
81	  return tab
82	}
83	```
84	
85	Update `hasLiveRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:2257`) to also check live Investigate tabs, reusing
86	the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:
87	
88	```swift
89	var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
90	  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
91	    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
92	      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
93	    }
94	}
95	```
96	
97	In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
98	its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
99	doesn't linger:
100	
101	```swift
102	ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
103	```
104	
105	Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
106	run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
107	has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
108	alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
109	process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.
110	
111	### 2. `TerminalStatusBar.swift:326-332` — route through the new method
112	
113	Replace the direct `addRunTab` call in the `onInvestigate` closure:
114	
115	```swift
116	onInvestigate: {
117	  let cwd = state?.view.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
118	  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: bannerState, target: target, cwd: cwd)
119	  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tabID)
120	  showingDiagnosis = false
121	},
122	```
123	
124	(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here.)
125	
126	### 3. `TerminalTabStrip.swift:436-441` — fix bug 2 and route through the new method
127	
128	Replace the hardcoded `"claude"` + direct `addRunTab` call:
129	
130	```swift
131	onInvestigate: {
132	  let cwd = tab.surface?.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
133	  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: state, target: target, cwd: cwd)
134	  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tab.id)
135	  agentPopoverTab = nil
136	},
137	```
138	
139	(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here; `state` is the `AgentBannerState`
140	already bound by the enclosing `if let state = agentManager.banners[tab.id]`. `tab.surface`
141	(`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) already collapses the `if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content`
142	match — no need to hand-roll it again, matching the status-bar site's `state?.view` shape.)
143	
144	This fixes bug 2 (both sites now build the identical seeded command via
145	`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`) and closes bug 1 (both sites now go through
146	`AppStore`, which owns the tracking, restoring `addRunTab`'s documented caller contract).
147	
148	**Drive-by cleanup, same file:** the neighboring `onInsertFix` closure (line ~434) has the exact
149	pattern-match `onInvestigate` used to have — `if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content { s.view.sendText(fix) }`.
150	Since the Code Quality fix above already replaces that pattern with `tab.surface` one closure
151	down, swap this line too so the file doesn't have the old form sitting right above the new one:
152	
153	```swift
154	onInsertFix: { fix in
155	  tab.surface?.sendText(fix)
156	  agentPopoverTab = nil
157	},
158	```
159	
160	Unrelated to issue #146's two bugs — spotted incidentally while fixing the Code Quality finding
161	above, folded in because it's a one-line, same-file, zero-risk consistency fix (not deferred to
162	TODOS.md).
163	
164	### 4. `TerminalSessions.swift:945-952` — doc note
165	
166	Add one line to `addRunTab`'s doc comment noting Investigate sessions are tracked in
167	`AppStore.investigateTabs`, not `runStates`, so the split is explicit at the definition too (not
168	just at the call sites) — closes the issue's "or a comment explaining why" fallback for the part
169	that *is* staying a deliberate design choice (no cross-window dedup, no supervisor/pidfile).
170	
171	## Verification
172	
173	- `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests.swift` — add:
174	  - A test asserting `startInvestigate` produces a tab whose command matches
175	    `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` for a given `AgentBannerState`, and that
176	    `investigateTabs[tab.id] == target.id` afterward — covers "both call sites build the same
177	    command line" (the issue's suggested unit check) by construction, since both now call the
178	    one method.
179	  - A test that `hasLiveRunCommand` is `false` before `startInvestigate`, `true` while the tab's
180	    surface reports a live process, and `false` again after simulating `onChildExited` and
181	    (separately) after simulating tab removal — two independent cleanup paths, both must be
182	    tested (mirrors the existing `testGracefullyStopAllWaitsForEveryLiveCommandThenCompletes` /
183	    `testReapClearsRunState` style already in this file).
184	  - A test that `gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` completes immediately (no hang) when the only
185	    live process is an Investigate tab and `runStates` is empty — this exact combination

194	  - Start Investigate, then close the *window* (⌘W the window / red close button, not the tab)

232	[+] Investigate from status bar / tab-strip
233	  ├── [★★  MANUAL] Fail a command → open Investigate from both sites → both seed
234	  │     the same prompt (not a bare `claude`)

239	QUALITY: ★★★:6  |  GAPS: 0

242	**Fast path:** all identified code paths and user flows have test coverage (unit or manual). No
243	regression rule triggers beyond what's already folded into the plan (bug 2's fix has no existing
244	test pinning the buggy behavior, so the new unit test IS the regression guard going forward).
245	
246	## Failure modes
247	
248	| Codepath | Realistic failure | Tested? | Error handling? | User-visible or silent? |
249	|---|---|---|---|---|
250	| `startInvestigate` → `addRunTab` | Surface fails to spawn (`tab.surface?.didSpawnFail`) | No | None added (matches Investigate's pre-existing behavior — never had spawn-failure handling) | **Visible** — the tab focuses immediately (unlike a backgrounded dev-server run), so the user sees the failure directly in the pane |

252	| Tab closes and process exits in the same tick | Both cleanup paths (`onChildExited` and `onTabsRemoved`) fire for the same tab id | No dedicated test, but `Dictionary.removeValue(forKey:)` on an absent key is a safe no-op | N/A — idempotent by construction | N/A |

260	  modeled on (create tab → wire `onChildExited` → track ownership).
261	- `AppStore.liveRunView`'s `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` idiom — reused
262	  verbatim inside the new `hasLiveRunCommand` clause instead of inventing a second way to ask
263	  "is this tab's process alive."
264	- `onTabsRemoved`'s existing `runStates` purge block — extended with a sibling line rather than
265	  building a separate removal mechanism.
266	- `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` — already existed and was already correct; the bug
267	  was that one call site never called it.
268	- `TerminalTab.surface` (`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) — reused in the `TerminalTabStrip` fix
269	  instead of re-deriving the same pattern-match a third time in the codebase.
270	
271	Nothing in this plan rebuilds a flow that already exists — every new line either reuses an
272	established accessor/pattern or is genuinely new bookkeeping (`investigateTabs` itself, which has
273	no existing equivalent since Investigate was previously untracked entirely).
274	
275	## NOT in scope
276	
277	- **Widening `RunState`/`runStates` to support multiple tabs per target.** Rejected in favor of a
278	  separate `investigateTabs` record (see Context) — `RunState` and `WindowRegistry.runOwner` are
279	  purpose-built for a single dev-server-style run per target, and an Investigate session must not
280	  inherit that single-slot/cross-window-dedup semantics.
281	- **Sending a live Investigate tab a graceful stop signal on quit** (mirroring how
282	  `gracefullyStopRuns` Ctrl-C's-and-waits for a dev-server run command). Discussed and rejected —
283	  quit already shows an unconditional "stops any running processes" confirm alert regardless of
284	  what's running (`WorkroomApp.swift:595-619`, not gated on `hasAnyLiveRunCommand`), and a killed
285	  Investigate session is resumable next launch via the existing `AgentResumeCoordinator`
286	  (`claude --resume`). Sending a stop signal and waiting for a "clean exit" also has no defined
287	  meaning for an interactive REPL the way it does for a dev server releasing a port. Not logged as
288	  a TODO — the user-facing concern is already soft-landed twice over (blanket dialog + resume).
289	- **Cross-window dedup for Investigate sessions.** `WindowRegistry.runOwner` deliberately continues
290	  to see only `runStates` — two windows investigating the same target concurrently is intended
291	  behavior, not a gap.
292	- **Spawn-failure handling (outcome/toast) for a failed Investigate launch.** Investigate never had
293	  this; adding it now would be scope creep beyond what issue #146 asked for, and the failure is
294	  already visible to the user (see Failure modes).
295	
296	## Worktree parallelization strategy
297	
298	Sequential implementation, no parallelization opportunity — every change centers on the single new
299	`AppStore.startInvestigate` method and its two call sites; the `TerminalSessions.swift` doc line
300	and the test file are small enough that splitting them into separate worktrees would cost more in
301	coordination than it saves.
302	
303	## Implementation Tasks
304	
305	Synthesized from this review's findings. Each task derives from a specific finding above. Run
306	with Claude Code, checkbox as you ship.

316	  - Files: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift`
317	  - Verify: manual Investigate click still seeds the correct prompt
318	- [ ] **T3 (P1, human: ~20min / CC: ~5min)** — TerminalTabStrip — fix bug 2 (hardcoded `"claude"`),
319	      route through `store.startInvestigate`, use `tab.surface` instead of hand-rolled match in
320	      both `onInvestigate` and the neighboring `onInsertFix` (drive-by consistency fix)
321	  - Surfaced by: issue #146 bug 2 + Code Quality review (DRY finding)
322	  - Files: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift`
323	  - Verify: manual Investigate click from tab-strip popover now seeds the failure prompt

# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites

## Context

Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").

**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
is still a real (if minor) UX gap.

**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.

The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.

## Changes

### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point

Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
`RunState`:

```swift
/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
/// SIGHUP'ing it.
///
///        runStates                    investigateTabs
///   [TargetID: RunState]          [TabID: TargetID]
///   one slot per target      many tabs allowed per target
///   (dev-server run)              (interactive claude)
///            │                            │
///            └─────────────┬──────────────┘
///                          ▼
///               hasLiveRunCommand (OR)
///                          │
///              ┌───────────┴────────────┐
///              ▼                        ▼
///   windowShouldClose confirm   stopRunCommandsThenTerminate (⌘Q)
///   alert — now fires for a     — unaffected in practice: only
///   live Investigate session    `runStates` feeds the actual
///                                gracefully-stop loop
@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
```

Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
both views will call:

```swift
/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
@discardableResult
func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
  -> TerminalTab
{
  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
  }
  return tab
}
```

Update `hasLiveRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:2257`) to also check live Investigate tabs, reusing
the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:

```swift
var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
    }
}
```

In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
doesn't linger:

```swift
ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
```

Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.

### 2. `TerminalStatusBar.swift:326-332` — route through the new method

Replace the direct `addRunTab` call in the `onInvestigate` closure:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd = state?.view.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: bannerState, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tabID)
  showingDiagnosis = false
},
```

(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here.)

### 3. `TerminalTabStrip.swift:436-441` — fix bug 2 and route through the new method

Replace the hardcoded `"claude"` + direct `addRunTab` call:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd = tab.surface?.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: state, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tab.id)
  agentPopoverTab = nil
},
```

(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here; `state` is the `AgentBannerState`
already bound by the enclosing `if let state = agentManager.banners[tab.id]`. `tab.surface`
(`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) already collapses the `if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content`
match — no need to hand-roll it again, matching the status-bar site's `state?.view` shape.)

This fixes bug 2 (both sites now build the identical seeded command via
`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`) and closes bug 1 (both sites now go through
`AppStore`, which owns the tracking, restoring `addRunTab`'s documented caller contract).

**Drive-by cleanup, same file:** the neighboring `onInsertFix` closure (line ~434) has the exact
pattern-match `onInvestigate` used to have — `if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content { s.view.sendText(fix) }`.
Since the Code Quality fix above already replaces that pattern with `tab.surface` one closure
down, swap this line too so the file doesn't have the old form sitting right above the new one:

```swift
onInsertFix: { fix in
  tab.surface?.sendText(fix)
  agentPopoverTab = nil
},
```

Unrelated to issue #146's two bugs — spotted incidentally while fixing the Code Quality finding
above, folded in because it's a one-line, same-file, zero-risk consistency fix (not deferred to
TODOS.md).

### 4. `TerminalSessions.swift:945-952` — doc note

Add one line to `addRunTab`'s doc comment noting Investigate sessions are tracked in
`AppStore.investigateTabs`, not `runStates`, so the split is explicit at the definition too (not
just at the call sites) — closes the issue's "or a comment explaining why" fallback for the part
that *is* staying a deliberate design choice (no cross-window dedup, no supervisor/pidfile).

## Verification

- `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests.swift` — add:
  - A test asserting `startInvestigate` produces a tab whose command matches
    `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` for a given `AgentBannerState`, and that
    `investigateTabs[tab.id] == target.id` afterward — covers "both call sites build the same
    command line" (the issue's suggested unit check) by construction, since both now call the
    one method.
  - A test that `hasLiveRunCommand` is `false` before `startInvestigate`, `true` while the tab's
    surface reports a live process, and `false` again after simulating `onChildExited` and
    (separately) after simulating tab removal — two independent cleanup paths, both must be
    tested (mirrors the existing `testGracefullyStopAllWaitsForEveryLiveCommandThenCompletes` /
    `testReapClearsRunState` style already in this file).
  - A test that `gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` completes immediately (no hang) when the only
    live process is an Investigate tab and `runStates` is empty — this exact combination
    (`hasLiveRunCommand == true` via `investigateTabs`, but nothing in `runStates` to iterate) is
    new with this change; the existing `testGracefullyStopAllCompletesImmediatelyWhenNothingLive`
    only covers the "nothing at all is live" case.
- `make app-lint` / `make app-format` on the touched files.
- `make app-test` (or scoped `xcodebuild -only-testing:WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests`) green.
- Manual, per the issue's own verification section:
  - Fail a command, open Investigate from the status bar and from the tab-strip chip — confirm
    both agents start with the failure context (the prompt text, not a bare `claude`).
  - Start Investigate, then close the *window* (⌘W the window / red close button, not the tab)
    with "confirm on quit" enabled — confirm the close-confirmation now fires for the live agent
    instead of silently killing it. **Note:** ⌘Q (app quit) needs no separate check here —
    `applicationShouldTerminate` (`WorkroomApp.swift:595-619`) already shows an *unconditional*
    "Quit Workroom? Quitting closes all terminals and stops any running processes." alert whenever
    `confirmOnQuit` is on, regardless of `hasAnyLiveRunCommand`, so a live Investigate session is
    already covered by that blanket warning today. What quit does NOT do, before or after this
    plan, is send an Investigate tab any graceful stop signal (`gracefullyStopRuns` only touches
    `runStates`) — see "NOT in scope" for why that's left alone.

## Test coverage diagram

```

  ├── startInvestigate(bannerState:target:cwd:)  [NEW]

  │     └── [★★★ TESTED] covered by the tab-removal case above

        └── [★★★ TESTED] completes immediately when only an Investigate tab is live
            (runStates empty) — the one NEW combination existing tests don't hit

[+] TerminalStatusBar.swift — onInvestigate closure  [MODIFIED: routes through startInvestigate]
  └── [★★★ TESTED] by construction — no per-view logic left to diverge; the shared
      method's test above is the regression guard for both call sites

[+] TerminalTabStrip.swift — onInvestigate closure  [MODIFIED: fixes bug 2, uses tab.surface]
  └── [★★★ TESTED] by construction, same reasoning — this is also the regression test

[+] Investigate from status bar / tab-strip
```

**Fast path:** all identified code paths and user flows have test coverage (unit or manual). No
regression rule triggers beyond what's already folded into the plan (bug 2's fix has no existing
test pinning the buggy behavior, so the new unit test IS the regression guard going forward).

## Failure modes

| Codepath | Realistic failure | Tested? | Error handling? | User-visible or silent? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `startInvestigate` → `addRunTab` | Surface fails to spawn (`tab.surface?.didSpawnFail`) | No | None added (matches Investigate's pre-existing behavior — never had spawn-failure handling) | **Visible** — the tab focuses immediately (unlike a backgrounded dev-server run), so the user sees the failure directly in the pane |
| `onChildExited` never fires (known libghostty exit-reporting flakiness) | `investigateTabs` entry could linger | Yes (indirectly, via the tab-removal test) | `onTabsRemoved`'s purge is a second, independent cleanup path that doesn't depend on `onChildExited` firing | Not silent — worst case is a stale dict entry until the tab closes, with no observable effect (the entry only feeds a liveness check that also reads the surface's actual `hasLiveProcess`) |
| Tab closes and process exits in the same tick | Both cleanup paths (`onChildExited` and `onTabsRemoved`) fire for the same tab id | No dedicated test, but `Dictionary.removeValue(forKey:)` on an absent key is a safe no-op | N/A — idempotent by construction | N/A |

No critical gaps (no path is simultaneously untested, unhandled, and silent).

## What already exists

- `TerminalSessions.addRunTab` — reused as-is; not modified beyond a doc-comment line.
- `AppStore.startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` — the existing pattern `startInvestigate` is
  modeled on (create tab → wire `onChildExited` → track ownership).
- `AppStore.liveRunView`'s `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` idiom — reused
  verbatim inside the new `hasLiveRunCommand` clause instead of inventing a second way to ask
  "is this tab's process alive."
- `onTabsRemoved`'s existing `runStates` purge block — extended with a sibling line rather than
  building a separate removal mechanism.
- `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` — already existed and was already correct; the bug
  was that one call site never called it.
- `TerminalTab.surface` (`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) — reused in the `TerminalTabStrip` fix
  instead of re-deriving the same pattern-match a third time in the codebase.

Nothing in this plan rebuilds a flow that already exists — every new line either reuses an
established accessor/pattern or is genuinely new bookkeeping (`investigateTabs` itself, which has
no existing equivalent since Investigate was previously untracked entirely).

## NOT in scope

- **Widening `RunState`/`runStates` to support multiple tabs per target.** Rejected in favor of a
  separate `investigateTabs` record (see Context) — `RunState` and `WindowRegistry.runOwner` are
  purpose-built for a single dev-server-style run per target, and an Investigate session must not
  inherit that single-slot/cross-window-dedup semantics.
- **Sending a live Investigate tab a graceful stop signal on quit** (mirroring how
  `gracefullyStopRuns` Ctrl-C's-and-waits for a dev-server run command). Discussed and rejected —
  quit already shows an unconditional "stops any running processes" confirm alert regardless of
  what's running (`WorkroomApp.swift:595-619`, not gated on `hasAnyLiveRunCommand`), and a killed
  Investigate session is resumable next launch via the existing `AgentResumeCoordinator`

  meaning for an interactive REPL the way it does for a dev server releasing a port. Not logged as
  a TODO — the user-facing concern is already soft-landed twice over (blanket dialog + resume).
- **Cross-window dedup for Investigate sessions.** `WindowRegistry.runOwner` deliberately continues
  to see only `runStates` — two windows investigating the same target concurrently is intended
  behavior, not a gap.
- **Spawn-failure handling (outcome/toast) for a failed Investigate launch.** Investigate never had
  this; adding it now would be scope creep beyond what issue #146 asked for, and the failure is
  already visible to the user (see Failure modes).

Sequential implementation, no parallelization opportunity — every change centers on the single new
`AppStore.startInvestigate` method and its two call sites; the `TerminalSessions.swift` doc line
and the test file are small enough that splitting them into separate worktrees would cost more in
coordination than it saves.

THE PLAN:
# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites

## Context

Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").

**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
is still a real (if minor) UX gap.

**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.

The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.

## Changes

### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point

Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
`RunState`:

```swift
/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
/// SIGHUP'ing it.
///
///        runStates                    investigateTabs
///   [TargetID: RunState]          [TabID: TargetID]
///   one slot per target      many tabs allowed per target
///   (dev-server run)              (interactive claude)
///            │                            │
///            └─────────────┬──────────────┘
///                          ▼
///               hasLiveRunCommand (OR)
///                          │
```

Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
both views will call:

```swift
/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
@discardableResult
func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
  -> TerminalTab
{
  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
  }
  return tab
}
```

```swift
  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
    }
}
```


Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session

alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the

## What already exists

- `TerminalSessions.addRunTab` — reused as-is; not modified beyond a doc-comment line.
- `AppStore.startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` — the existing pattern `startInvestigate` is
  modeled on (create tab → wire `onChildExited` → track ownership).
- `AppStore.liveRunView`'s `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` idiom — reused
  verbatim inside the new `hasLiveRunCommand` clause instead of inventing a second way to ask
  "is this tab's process alive."
- `onTabsRemoved`'s existing `runStates` purge block — extended with a sibling line rather than
  building a separate removal mechanism.
- `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` — already existed and was already correct; the bug
  was that one call site never called it.
- `TerminalTab.surface` (`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) — reused in the `TerminalTabStrip` fix
  instead of re-deriving the same pattern-match a third time in the codebase.

Nothing in this plan rebuilds a flow that already exists — every new line either reuses an
established accessor/pattern or is genuinely new bookkeeping (`investigateTabs` itself, which has
no existing equivalent since Investigate was previously untracked entirely).

## NOT in scope

- **Widening `RunState`/`runStates` to support multiple tabs per target.** Rejected in favor of a
  separate `investigateTabs` record (see Context) — `RunState` and `WindowRegistry.runOwner` are
  purpose-built for a single dev-server-style run per target, and an Investigate session must not
  inherit that single-slot/cross-window-dedup semantics.
- **Sending a live Investigate tab a graceful stop signal on quit** (mirroring how
  `gracefullyStopRuns` Ctrl-C's-and-waits for a dev-server run command). Discussed and rejected —
  quit already shows an unconditional "stops any running processes" confirm alert regardless of
  what's running (`WorkroomApp.swift:595-619`, not gated on `hasAnyLiveRunCommand`), and a killed
  Investigate session is resumable next launch via the existing `AgentResumeCoordinator`
  (`claude --resume`). Sending a stop signal and waiting for a "clean exit" also has no defined
  meaning for an interactive REPL the way it does for a dev server releasing a port. Not logged as
  a TODO — the user-facing concern is already soft-landed twice over (blanket dialog + resume).
- **Cross-window dedup for Investigate sessions.** `WindowRegistry.runOwner` deliberately continues
  to see only `runStates` — two windows investigating the same target concurrently is intended
  behavior, not a gap.
- **Spawn-failure handling (outcome/toast) for a failed Investigate launch.** Investigate never had
  this; adding it now would be scope creep beyond what issue #146 asked for, and the failure is
  already visible to the user (see Failure modes).

## Worktree parallelization strategy

Sequential implementation, no parallelization opportunity — every change centers on the single new
`AppStore.startInvestigate` method and its two call sites; the `TerminalSessions.swift` doc line
and the test file are small enough that splitting them into separate worktrees would cost more in
coordination than it saves.

71	value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
72	(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
73	must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
74	Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
75	call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.

77	## Changes

79	### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point
80	
81	Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
82	`RunState`:

84	```swift
85	/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
86	/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
87	/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
88	/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
89	/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
90	/// SIGHUP'ing it.
91	///
92	///        runStates                    investigateTabs
93	///   [TargetID: RunState]          [TabID: TargetID]
94	///   one slot per target      many tabs allowed per target
95	///   (dev-server run)              (interactive claude)
96	///            │                            │
97	///            └─────────────┬──────────────┘
98	///                          ▼
99	///               hasLiveRunCommand (OR)
100	///                          │
101	///              ┌───────────┴────────────┐
102	///              ▼                        ▼
103	///   windowShouldClose confirm   stopRunCommandsThenTerminate (⌘Q)
104	///   alert — now fires for a     — unaffected in practice: only
105	///   live Investigate session    `runStates` feeds the actual
106	///                                gracefully-stop loop
107	@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
108	```

111	both views will call:
112	
113	```swift
114	/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
115	/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
116	/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
117	@discardableResult
118	func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
119	  -> TerminalTab
120	{
121	  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
122	  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
123	  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
124	  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
125	    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
126	  }
127	  return tab
128	}
129	```

132	the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:
133	
134	```swift
135	var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
136	  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
137	    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
138	      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
139	    }
140	}
141	```

143	In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
144	its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
145	doesn't linger:
146	
147	```swift
148	ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
149	```

152	run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
153	has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
154	alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
155	process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.

# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites

## Context

Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").

**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
is still a real (if minor) UX gap.

**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.

The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.

## Changes

### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point

Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
`RunState`:

```swift
/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
/// SIGHUP'ing it.
///
///        runStates                    investigateTabs
///   [TargetID: RunState]          [TabID: TargetID]
///   one slot per target      many tabs allowed per target
///   (dev-server run)              (interactive claude)
///            │                            │
///            └─────────────┬──────────────┘
///                          ▼
///               hasLiveRunCommand (OR)
///                          │
///              ┌───────────┴────────────┐
///              ▼                        ▼
///   windowShouldClose confirm   stopRunCommandsThenTerminate (⌘Q)
///   alert — now fires for a     — unaffected in practice: only
///   live Investigate session    `runStates` feeds the actual
///                                gracefully-stop loop
@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
```

Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
both views will call:

```swift
/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
@discardableResult
func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
  -> TerminalTab
{
  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
  }
  return tab
}
```

Update `hasLiveRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:2257`) to also check live Investigate tabs, reusing
the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:

```swift
var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
    }
}
```

In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
doesn't linger:

```swift
ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
```

Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.

Replace the direct `addRunTab` call in the `onInvestigate` closure:

1. `WindowRegistry.gracefullyStopAllWindows` (`WindowRegistry.swift:223`) — filters stores by

   only live thing is an Investigate tab, that call iterates `runStates.keys` (empty) and resolves
   immediately — covered by the "no-hang" unit test below.
2. `windowShouldClose` (`WindowRegistry.swift:254`) — the fix's actual target; now correctly gates
   the confirm alert on a live Investigate session too.
3. `stopRunCommandsThenTerminate` (`WorkroomApp.swift:640`) — decides sync-`.terminateNow` vs the
   async graceful-dance; flips to the async path for an Investigate-only session, which (per #1)
   resolves near-instantly. No hang, no new behavior beyond the harmless extra tick.
None of the three assumes "true ⟹ present in `runStates` and gracefully-stoppable" in a way that
breaks — each one either doesn't care (windowShouldClose) or safely no-ops when `runStates` doesn't
contain the tab (the other two).
